Arrow's Theorem

Switch preference profiles and aggregation rules. On the Condorcet profile majority rule cycles; under Borda, removing an irrelevant alternative flips the ranking (IIA violation). No rule satisfies all four conditions.

no rule satisfies U + P + IIA + non-dictatorship\text{no rule satisfies U + P + IIA + non-dictatorship}no rule satisfies U + P + IIA + non-dictatorship

Examples & Exercises

For the profile (1: A>B>CA > B > CA>B>C, 2: B>C>AB > C > AB>C>A, 3: C>A>BC > A > BC>A>B), show by direct computation that pairwise majority cycles.

A>B,B>C,C>AA > B,\quad B > C,\quad C > AA>B,B>C,C>A
Show proof
  1. AAA vs BBB: voters 1 and 3 support A>BA > BA>B, so A>BA > BA>B (2–1).
  2. BBB vs CCC: voters 1 and 2 have B>CB > CB>C, so B>CB > CB>C (2–1). CCC vs AAA: voters 2 and 3 have C>AC > AC>A, so C>AC > AC>A (2–1). Hence A>B>C>AA > B > C > AA>B>C>A cycles — pairwise majority yields no transitive ranking.

For the profile (1, 2: B>A>CB > A > CB>A>C, 3: A>C>BA > C > BA>C>B), compute Borda scores and show how the AAA–BBB order changes when CCC is removed (IIA violation).

full: A=B=4,without C: B=2>1=A\text{full: } A = B = 4,\quad \text{without } C\text{: } B = 2 > 1 = Afull: A=B=4,without C: B=2>1=A
Show proof
  1. Full Borda scores (2/1/0): A=1+1+2=4A = 1+1+2 = 4A=1+1+2=4, B=2+2+0=4B = 2+2+0 = 4B=2+2+0=4, C=0+0+1=1C = 0+0+1 = 1C=0+0+1=1 — AAA and BBB tie.
  2. Without CCC (1/0): B=1+1+0=2B = 1+1+0 = 2B=1+1+0=2, A=0+0+1=1A = 0+0+1 = 1A=0+0+1=1 — BBB wins. Removing the irrelevant alternative CCC changed the AAA–BBB ranking, violating IIA.
